Inglewood, California
  January 15, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  January 15, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority and Parking Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
  Authority Secretary and Parking Authority Secretary announced the presence of a
  quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman and Parking
  Authority Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/ Finance
  Authority Members/Parking Authority Members Dotson,
  Padilla, Morales and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority and Parking Authority
  officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Wanda Brown  City Treasurer/Treasurer*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Patricia McNish  Management Assistant

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority
  and Parking Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Finance Authority Chairman and Parking
  Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to
  address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority and
  Parking Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member /
  Successor Agency Member /Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  ,January 7, 2019, in the amount of $1,107,853.86, and dated January 10, 2019, in the
  amount of $2,421,969.12 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 19-06 INTRODUCED -
  ADOPTING THE 2016 CALIFORNIA TITLE 24 BUILDING CODES BY
  AMENDING AND DELETING VARIOUS SECTIONS AND ARTICLES OF
  CHAPTER 11 (BUILDING REGULATIONS), OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE.

  1
 January 15, 2019

  The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a Public Hearing to consider an
  Ordinance adopting the 2016 California Title 24 Building Codes by amending and
  deleting various sections and articles of Chapter 11 (Building Regulations), of the
  Inglewood Municipal Code, and that notice had been given in the time, form and manner
  as required by law, an affidavit was on file and no communication were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the staff report dated January 15, 2019.

  Mandhir Singh, Building Official gave a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council.

  There was no response.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by
  Council Member Franklin that the City Council does hereby waive further reading. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 19-06 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  ADOPTING THE 2016 CALIFORNIA TITLE 24 BUILDING CODES BY
  AMENDING AND DELETING VARIOUS SECTIONS AND ARTICLES OF
  CHAPTER 11 (BUILDING REGULATIONS), OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE

  was introduced by Mayor Butts.

 132  CLAIMS DENIED.  Letters from the Office of the City Attorney were received
  recommending denial of the following claims:
  a) Shelle Kirk for alleged property damage on November 26, 2018.
  b) George Williams for alleged property damage on October 17, 2018.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  and carried that the above listed claim be denied.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on November 27,
  2018, and December 4, 2018, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 178  PAYMENT APPROVED – QUEST DIAGNOSTICS; PAYMENT OF
  ADDITIONAL INVOICES SUBMITTED BY QUEST DIAGNOSTICS
  AUTHORIZED. Staff Report dated January 15, 2019, was presented recommending
  approval to pay invoices submitted by Quest Diagnostics for providing random drug
  testing to sworn Police personnel.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby 1) Approve payment in the amount of $1,852; and 2)
  Authorize payment of additional invoices, in an amount up to $7,500 upon submittal. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
 January 15, 2019

 103.3  AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-080 APPROVED – KARABUILD
  DEVELOPMENT, INC. Staff Report dated January 15, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of an amendment to Agreement No. 18-080 with Karabuild
  Development, Inc., extending the term to March 31, 2019, to complete the residential
  sound insulation work on 45 homes (RSI PHASE XV, GROUP 7).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve an Amendment to Agreement No. 18-080 with
  Karabuild Development, Inc. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 103.3  AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-081 APPROVED – KARABUILD
  DEVELOPMENT, INC. Staff Report dated January 15, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of an amendment to Agreement No. 18-081 with Karabuild
  Development, Inc., extending the term to March 31, 2019, to complete the residential
  sound insulation work on 49 homes (RSI PHASE XV, GROUP 8).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve an Amendment to Agreement No. 18-081 with
  Karabuild Development, Inc. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 101  RESOLUTION NO. 19-024/CSA 19-01 ADOPTED -  APPROVING THE
  RECOGNIZED OBLIGATION PAYMENT SCHEDULE (ROPS) FOR JULY 1,
  2019 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2020; - RESOLUTION NO. 19-025/CSA 19-02
  ADOPTED – APPROVING THE ADMINISTRATIVE ALLOWANCE BUDGET
  FOR THE ROPS PERIOD FROM JULY 1, 2019 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2020
  (ROPS) AND AUTHORIZING STAFF TO SUBMIT ROPS TO DISTRICT
  CONSOLIDATED OVERSIGHT BOARD. Staff report dated January 15, 2019, was
  presented recommending adoption of a resolution to approve the July 1, 2019 through
  June 30, 2020, Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule (ROPS19-20) for the
  expenditure of Redevelopment Property Tax Trust Funds (RPTTF) for submittal to the
  Second Supervisorial District Consolidated Oversight Board (“Consolidated Oversight
  Board”) for approval consideration.

  It was moved by Council Member /Successor Agency Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member Dotson that the City Council/Successor
  Agency does hereby 1) Adopt Resolution No. 19-024/CSA 19-01 entitled:

  A RESOLUTON OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD AS SUCCESSOR
  AGENCY TO THE FORMER INGLEWOOD REDEVELOPMENT
  AGENCY APPROVING THE RECOGNIZED OBLIGATION
  PAYMENT SCHEDULE (ROPS) FOR JULY 1, 2019 THROUGH JUNE
  30, 2020 (19-20) PURSUANT TO HEALTH & SAFETY CODE
  SECTION 34177 (O)(1)(E) AND AUTHORIZING STAFF TO SUBMIT
  THE ROPS TO THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY SECOND
  SUPERVISORIAL DISTRICT CONSOLIDATED OVERSIGHT
  BOARD

  and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 19-025/CSA19-02 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD AS SUCCESSOR
  AGENCY TO THE FORMER INGLEWOOD REDEVELOPMENT
  AGENCY APPROVING THE ADMINISTRATIVE ALLOWANCE
  BUDGET FOR THE ROPS PERIOD FROM JULY 1, 2019 THROUGH
  JUNE 30, 2020 (ROPS 19-20); AND AUTHORIZING STAFF TO
  SUBMIT THE ROPS TO THE SECOND SUPERVISORIAL DISTRICT
  CONSOLIDATED OVERSIGHT BOARD

  3
 January 15, 2019

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin
  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  132.6  CLOSED SESSION – STEPHANIE FITZPATRICK  VS. THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD. Closed session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; City
  Council Conference with Legal Counsel regarding Anticipated Litigation Pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2); Workers Compensation Claims of Stephanie
  Fitzpatrick: Claim No. 16-125844, ADJ No. 10407084; and Claim No. 16-126312, ADJ
  No. 10407083.
  This Item was pulled from the Agenda.
  126  REMARKS - CITY CLERK. Yvonne Horton, City Clerk, stated that she and the Los
  Angeles Registrar Recorders Office met with residents of Inglewood to discuss and
  explain the upcoming Voters Centers. The City Clerk thanked the residents for their
  strong turn out and also noted that the Representatives from Los Angeles County
  Registrar Recorder’s Office commented that the meeting in the City of Inglewood was
  one of the best.

 219  CITY TREASURER – MONTHLY TREASURER’S REPORT. Staff report dated
  January 15, 2019, was presented submitting the Monthly Treasurer’s Report for the
  Month ending October 31, 2018.

  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

 219  REMARKS – CITY TREASURER. Wanda Brown, City Treasurer, reported on the
  City’s investments and interest earnings. The City Treasurer also stated that she attended
  a Treasurers Conference in Palm Springs, California on January 8th - 11th, 2019, which
  included sessions on pension reform.
  .
  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Ray Davis thanked the Mayor for being proactive on the rent increases throughout the
  City. He also stated that a lot of changes for the better are being made throughout the
  City.

  No Name Given, stated that HBO (Home Box Office) will be hosting a free screening of
  “King in the Wilderness” at Miracle Theatre on Saturday, January 19, 2019, in honor the
  of the Martin Luther King , Jr. celebration.

  Stuart Bailey thanked the Council Members for their Toy Giveaways held in December
  which he acknowledged were a success. He also thanked the City Council and the City
  Clerk for supporting each other’s events.

  Frances Taylor thanked and congratulated the Los Angeles County Fire Department, and
  the Inglewood Police Department for their services to all the families affected by the
  Building fire on Queen Street. The fire destroyed two cars and one family’s apartment.
  Mr. Taylor encouraged the residents to obtain Renters Insurance.

  Jim Vaughn shouted “GO RAMS!” for the upcoming Playoff Game to be played on
  Sunday, January 20, 2019.

  4
 January 15, 2019

  MAYOR BUTTS STATED FOR CLARIFICATION THAT HE WANTED TO
  ENSURE THAT BOTH RECOMMENDATIONS FOR AGENDA ITEM NO.
  7&CSA2 WERE APPROVED.

  It was moved by Council Member/Successor Agency Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member Franklin that the City Council/Successor
  Agency does hereby move that the two recommendations for Item No. 7&CSA2 be
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Succesor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin
  and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at 2:23 p.m.

  Approved this 5th day of February, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
